links.label: grew out of blues
links.reason: New Orleans jazz mixed brass-band marches, ragtime and blues with group improvisation, and blues forms and blue notes stayed at its heart.

links.label: grew out of blues
links.reason: Rhythm and blues was shaped by blending blues and jazz with a city sound.

links.label: grew out of blues
links.reason: Chicago electric blues supplied many of rock and roll's elements, and its 12-bar form runs through early hits.

links.label: grew out of blues
links.reason: Rock borrowed the verse-refrain shape of blues, and British bands like the Rolling Stones drew directly on American blues.

links.label: grew out of jazz
links.reason: Rhythm and blues was shaped by blending jazz and blues with a city sound.

links.label: grew out of jazz
links.reason: Funk can be placed in a line running from rhythm and blues, jazz and soul.

links.label: drew on jazz
links.reason: Reggae's precursors drew on American jazz and rhythm and blues alongside Jamaican music.

links.label: jazz met samba
links.reason: Bossa nova took some harmony and instrumentation from jazz, though its rich chords also grew out of samba guitar on a parallel path.

links.label: jazz met salsa
links.reason: Salsa folds in jazz alongside mambo, rumba, bolero and R&B.

links.label: jazz met afrobeat
links.reason: Afrobeat carries American funk, jazz and soul influences.

links.label: grew out of gospel
links.reason: Rhythm and blues mixed gospel with jump blues, swing, boogie and blues, and its stronger gospel influence is what sets it apart from jump blues.

links.label: grew out of gospel
links.reason: Rock and roll's roots include rhythm and blues combined with shouting gospel.

links.label: grew out of gospel
links.reason: Soul music has its roots in African-American gospel music and rhythm and blues.

links.label: grew out of country
links.reason: Rock and roll mixed rhythm and blues with country music; rockabilly drew mainly on those country roots.

links.label: grew out of country
links.reason: Country is listed among rock's roots, alongside folk and rhythm and blues.

links.label: folk met rock
links.reason: Folk rock is usually thought to have taken off when the Byrds, from LA's folk café scene, recorded Dylan's 'Mr. Tambourine Man' with electric guitars and drums in 1965; Dylan went electric later that year.

links.label: grew out of R&B
links.reason: The immediate roots of rock and roll lay in rhythm and blues, then marketed as 'race music'.

links.label: grew out of rock and roll
links.reason: Rock music's foundations are in rock and roll, which by the mid-1960s had grown into a wider international style.

links.label: grew out of rock and roll
links.reason: Punk rock is rooted in 1950s rock and roll and 1960s garage rock.

links.label: grew out of rock
links.reason: Heavy metal is a genre of rock that grew from blues rock and psychedelic rock in the late 1960s.

sources.section: Soft rock, hard rock, and early heavy metal

links.label: pushed back against rock
links.reason: Punk bands rejected the overproduction and corporate feel of mainstream arena rock.

links.label: metal met alternative
links.reason: In the 1990s some bands were credited with making a place for heavy metal inside alternative rock.

links.label: alt-rock grew from punk
links.reason: Alternative rock describes the underground music that emerged in the wake of punk rock.

links.label: synth-pop arose from punk
links.reason: Synth-pop is said to have arisen partly from punk rock.

links.label: soul grew from R&B
links.reason: Soul is rooted in gospel and rhythm and blues, described by AllMusic as R&B made more urban and commercial.

links.label: funk grew from R&B
links.reason: Funk is placed in the lineage of rhythm and blues, jazz and soul, with its rhythmic template in New Orleans R&B.

links.label: reggae drew on R&B
links.reason: Jamaican music developed out of a mix of American R&B and the local mento style on the way to reggae.

links.label: salsa took in R&B
links.reason: Salsa is described as mixing Cuban styles with elements of jazz and R&B.

links.label: modern R&B grew from R&B
links.reason: Contemporary R&B, which developed in the late 1980s, combines rhythm and blues with pop, soul, funk, disco and electronic elements.

links.label: funk emerged from soul
links.reason: James Brown and Sly and the Family Stone moved from soul into funk, and funk vocals keep soul's approach.

links.label: disco grew from soul
links.reason: Philadelphia soul and psychedelic soul are named among disco's roots, and some early-1970s soul records are called a link to disco.

links.label: hip-hop draws on soul
links.reason: The Hip-hop infobox lists soul among the genre's stylistic origins.

links.label: Afrobeat took in soul
links.reason: Afrobeat mixes West African music with American funk, jazz and soul influences.

links.label: soul became modern R&B
links.reason: After the early 1980s soul grew slicker under electro's influence, becoming the style known as contemporary R&B.

links.label: disco drew on funk
links.reason: The Funk article says disco owed a great deal to funk, and the Disco infobox lists funk among its origins.

links.label: hip-hop sampled funk
links.reason: Hip-hop's earliest DJs drew mainly on disco and funk records, and funk breakbeats have been sampled widely ever since.

links.label: funk met African rhythm
links.reason: Exported to Africa, funk melded with African singing and rhythms, and Fela Kuti, heavily influenced by James Brown, is credited with creating Afrobeat.

links.label: electro grew from funk
links.reason: Electro emerged as a fusion of several styles, funk among them.

links.label: R&B folded in funk
links.reason: Contemporary R&B is described as rhythm and blues combined with elements of pop, disco, funk and soul.

links.label: house picked up disco
links.reason: House is described as picking up where disco left off at the end of the 1970s, with disco one of its main influences.

links.label: hip-hop sprang from disco
links.reason: Early Bronx DJs built hip-hop mainly from disco and funk records, and Chic's 'Good Times' became the basis of 'Rapper's Delight'. The Hip-hop article says much of the young genre's early spirit was a rebellion against disco, the music it came from.

links.label: synth-pop borrowed disco
links.reason: Synth-pop is described as drawing on disco and glam rock, forms critics looked down on.

links.label: techno built on disco
links.reason: Techno used the basic disco drum pattern as a foundation, and Italo and Euro disco were party staples in the Detroit scene it came from.

links.label: R&B folded in disco
links.reason: Contemporary R&B is described as rhythm and blues combined with elements of pop, disco, funk and soul.

links.label: garage borrowed R&B vocals
links.reason: UK garage's 2-step style added contemporary R&B-style vocals among its funkier elements.

links.label: R&B met hip-hop
links.reason: Teddy Riley's blend of R&B singing and hip-hop rhythms was named new jack swing, and the two genres have blended ever since.

links.label: remixed into dub
links.reason: Dub grew out of reggae as engineers stripped reggae tracks back to drums and bass and added echo and reverb.

links.label: via Spanish reggae
links.reason: Reggaeton evolved from dancehall and reggae, starting with the Spanish-language reggae of Panama in the late 1980s.

links.label: a digitised offshoot
links.reason: Jungle, the forerunner of drum and bass, has been called a raved-up, digitised offshoot of Jamaican reggae, and Britain's reggae culture helped form it.

links.label: toasting over versions
links.reason: The hip-hop article calls dub, with its vocal-free 'versions' of records, the strongest artistic precedent for hip-hop.

links.label: dub presaged ambient
links.reason: The ambient article names Jamaican dub among the styles that presaged ambient music, and the dub article lists ambient among the genres dub influenced.

links.label: a basis for jungle
links.reason: Dub was a basis for jungle and drum and bass.

links.label: bass and effects
links.reason: Dub was a major influence on dubstep, which shares its focus on bass and audio effects.

links.label: hip-hop meets dancehall
links.reason: Early producers DJ Playero and DJ Nelson were inspired by hip-hop and dancehall, and reggaeton songs follow hip-hop's verse-chorus-bridge structure.

links.label: trap grew out of hip-hop
links.reason: Trap is a subgenre of hip-hop that began in the Southern United States.

links.label: electro met rap
links.reason: Early electro was mostly instrumental but used rap, and electro in turn shaped hip-hop's new school.

links.label: drum and bass borrowed hip-hop
links.reason: Drum and bass drew on elements of reggae, dub and hip-hop.

links.label: trap drums in EDM
links.reason: From 2013 producers such as DJ Snake brought trap-influenced EDM into the mainstream, a fusion known as EDM trap.

links.label: techno-pop into electro
links.reason: Electro emerged as a fusion of funk and boogie with German and Japanese techno-pop, and lists synth-pop among its origins.

links.label: fed Detroit techno
links.reason: Juan Atkins and others developed Detroit techno from a style influenced by synth-pop and funk.

links.label: an influence on house
links.reason: Synth-pop was a major influence on house music, which grew out of early-1980s post-disco club culture.

links.label: Detroit electro roots
links.reason: Juan Atkins made electro as Cybotron before techno had its name, and many early British techno producers came to it through electro and hip hop.

links.label: electro in the mix
links.reason: House's infobox lists electro among its origins, and early Chicago DJs played electro funk by Afrika Bambaataa and Arthur Baker.

sources.section: 1980s: Chicago house, acid house and deep house

links.label: ambient breakdowns
links.reason: Trance incorporates influences from ambient, chill-out and film scores, and its breakdowns drop the beats to leave melody or atmosphere standing alone.

links.label: ambient techno
links.reason: Ambient techno, from the 1990s, set ambient atmospheres over the rhythms and melodies of techno.

links.label: ambient house chill-out
links.reason: Ambient house, from the late 1980s, added ambient atmospheres to acid house, as on chill-out albums like The KLF's Chill Out.

links.label: Chicago–Detroit kinship
links.reason: Detroit's techno producers were closely tied to the Chicago house scene, and German techno was described as a style built on Chicago house.

links.label: house and acid in trance
links.reason: Trance draws on house and acid house as well as techno.

links.label: New York garage, sped up
links.reason: UK garage grew in London from New York garage house, played faster in the second rooms of jungle nights.

links.label: house goes stadium
links.reason: The 2010s US 'EDM' sound was described as somewhere between electro and progressive house, and the Swedish house trio Swedish House Mafia is credited with setting the tone for the early-2010s EDM boom.

links.label: Frankfurt techno turns trance
links.reason: Trance emerged from the techno and EBM scene in Frankfurt in the late 1980s and early 1990s.

links.label: techno in the breakbeats
links.reason: Drum and bass drew on techno among many sources, and Kevin Saunderson's 'Reese' bassline became hugely influential in it.

links.label: jungle's second room
links.reason: UK garage grew partly out of jungle: the garage played in jungle nights' second rooms offered a slower, more soulful alternative.

links.label: drum and bass weight
links.reason: Early dubstep producers set out to bring drum and bass elements, like the bass drop, into the 2-step garage sound.

links.label: dark garage becomes dubstep
links.reason: Dubstep's roots are in the darker, more experimental B-sides of UK garage producers.

links.label: brostep crosses to America
links.reason: In 2011 dubstep took off in the US through Skrillex's harsher brostep, one of the sounds of the EDM boom.
